newsitem.title: ITALY: OECD expects Italian GDP growth of 1.3 pct in '97.
newsitem.headline: OECD expects Italian GDP growth of 1.3 pct in '97.

text.p: Italian gross domestic product (GDP) should grow by 1.3 percent in 1997, above government forecasts, with the economy strengthening further in 1998, the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) said.
Official statistics said the Italian economy grew just 0.7 percent last year after 2.9 percent growth in 1995. "Expansion has received an important setback," the OECD said in a report.

"The outlook is for a mild upturn in 1997, real GDP being projected to expand by 1.3 percent, led by stronger growth in export markets, but dampened by tighter fiscal policies and the lagged effects of recent exchange rate appreciation," it added.
As the impact of these two negative influences started to recede, GDP growth would climb to around 2.25 percent next year, the Paris-based organisation forecast.
The government has predicted GDP growth of 1.2 percent for this year and two percent in 1998.
"The slow pace of expansion may initially keep unemployment close to record levels," the report said.
It forecast that the unemployment rate would be 12.1 percent in 1997 and 11.8 percent in 1998. The high jobless total would help depress labour costs, it added.

"This, together with the (lira) re-entry into the ERM at a central rate which is likely to maintain a downward pressure on prices, will enable consumer price inflation to ease to around the official target rate of two percent in 1998," the OECD wrote.
The lira returned to the European Exchange Rate Mechanism last November at a central parity rate of 990 lire per Deutschemark. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
